primary_reader: Curious general nonfiction readers who enjoy surprising explanations of economics, data and everyday life, without needing economics, statistics or 1D3X knowledge.

reader_promise_territories.label: STRANGE_MEASURES
reader_promise_territories.promise: Ordinary objects can make enormous economic and social realities readable.
reader_promise_territories.commercial_strength: Strong curiosity and broad visual range.
reader_promise_territories.risk: Can become a list of trivia unless each story teaches a rule of measurement.

reader_promise_territories.label: HIDDEN_SIGNALS
reader_promise_territories.promise: Mundane products and flows can reveal changes before official numbers feel real.
reader_promise_territories.commercial_strength: Feels useful and current; fits markets, shipping, consumer behavior and nowcasting.
reader_promise_territories.risk: May sound like investing/business forecasting if subtitle is too narrow.

reader_promise_territories.label: MEASURE_MYTH
reader_promise_territories.promise: Some strange indicators illuminate the world; others are beautiful nonsense.
reader_promise_territories.commercial_strength: Adds skepticism, stakes and intellectual credibility.
reader_promise_territories.risk: Less instantly playful at thumbnail level.

packages.title: Burgers, Lipstick & Underwear
packages.subtitle: What everyday objects reveal about the economy
packages.reader_promise: A curious tour of the ordinary products people use to measure prices, confidence, purchasing power and hidden stress in the economy.
packages.main_risk: Economics may be invisible if the subtitle is weak.
packages.why_buy: It promises a fun, concrete popular-economics read from objects a shopper recognizes instantly.

packages.title: Signals in Strange Places
packages.subtitle: How burgers, freight and skyscrapers reveal what official numbers miss
packages.reader_promise: A guide to finding useful economic and social signals in mundane places, while learning which signals deserve skepticism.
packages.main_risk: Less object-funny than the list title; needs a vivid cover.
packages.why_buy: It sounds like useful explanatory nonfiction rather than a novelty list.

packages.title: Numbers You Can Feel
packages.subtitle: Cigarettes, burgers and everyday units that explain hidden systems
packages.reader_promise: A book about translating abstract numbers into familiar measures that readers can remember and question.
packages.main_risk: Concept-led title needs subtitle to carry the concrete hook.
packages.why_buy: It frames the book as emotionally legible data literacy, not technical economics.

packages.title: The Cigarette Index
packages.subtitle: Burgers, lattes and the strange measures that make the world readable
packages.reader_promise: A memorable entry point into strange measures, beginning with pollution translated into cigarette-equivalent exposure.
packages.main_risk: Cold shoppers may classify it as a smoking, tobacco, health or pollution book.
packages.why_buy: It has the sharpest single hook, but must be broadened immediately by subtitle and cover.

packages.title: The Weird Index
packages.subtitle: A guide to strange economic signals, useful myths and numbers that stick
packages.reader_promise: A broad guide to weird indicators and why some help while others mislead.
packages.main_risk: Generic, weakly ownable and already noisy as a web/product phrase.
packages.why_buy: Only works if the cover/subtitle do nearly all the commercial work.

packages.title: The Underwear Index
packages.subtitle: What hidden consumer signals reveal about markets, confidence and daily life
packages.reader_promise: A recession-signal hook used to explore consumer behavior and unofficial economic indicators.
packages.main_risk: Looks like a consumer-behavior, clothing or novelty/kids title rather than a broad economics/data book.
packages.why_buy: Powerful curiosity hook, but too narrow and too easy to misclassify.

recommendation.main_risk: Needs the subtitle and cover to make the economics/data promise unmistakable.
recommendation.mitigation: Use a subtitle with 'economy' or 'economic signals' and a cover hierarchy that shows ordinary objects connected by data/signal lines.

content_fit.cigarette_equivalent: strong fit but requires health/pollution disclaimer
content_fit.lipstick: strong curiosity fit, weak-evidence caution required
content_fit.mens_underwear: strong curiosity fit, weak-evidence caution required

luna_usage.work_replaced: bounded clustering sanity check over normalized corpus; final scoring and recommendation remain editorial judgment
